copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Friday, overnight UTC kickoff, brings Paraguay and Australia together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the Australia side, by +8.3pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

The Elo prior reads Paraguay 1730 vs Australia 1740: 10 points in favour of Australia, which is a meaningful but not decisive prior. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. The adjustment layer is quiet on this fixture — no host bonus, no home-ground correction, no altitude folding in. The Elo numbers above are what the model uses.

Three-way split from the model: Paraguay to win at 34%, the draw at 29%, and Australia to win at 36%. The away side reads 36% on this distribution — the model's central case for Australia.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Paraguay to win at 46%, the draw at 28%, and Australia to win at 28%. The Australia side trades at 28% on Polymarket, which prices out at American odds of +257. That's where the engine differs: our number reads 36%, +8.3pp wider.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Australia the lower bound is 31%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +3.3pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The Desk's posture is that calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures — we're not claiming the market is generally wrong, only that this side, on this fixture, looks mispriced. Selection is the dimension this verdict adds value on.

This number will move. Confirmed starting elevens, injuries, weather at the venue, and suspensions carried in from previous fixtures all re-enter the prior on the late-binding cadence. With kickoff roughly 35 days out, the model is on the weekly refresh cadence; we'll move to daily once we cross the T-5d window. The Pick can flip to a Pass if news moves enough of the prior. The Desk does not tip and does not recommend a trade — the model price, the market price, and the gap across them are what's on the page.
drivers: Pre-tournament Elo gives Australia a stronger prior than the Polymarket line implies.
The +8.3pp gap clears our 3 percentage point threshold for a Pick.
Calibration sits with the closing market across recent fixtures, so selection is the lever.
Late-binding signals — form, confirmed XI, weather — re-evaluate closer to kickoff.
copy.summary: The away side reads stronger to the model than to the market. Our Elo prior puts Australia at 36%; Polymarket prices that side at 28%. The +8.3pp gap calls a Pick.
copy.title: Paraguay v Australia · the model leans Australia
